articles.title: Why Can Cats See in the Dark?
articles.dek: Big pupils, special cells and a mirror inside the eye: discover a cat's night-time secret.

sources.name: Purina UK: Can cats see in the dark?

paras: Have you ever seen a cat in a garden at night? It walks around easily, but you can't see much at all. So why can cats see better than us in the dark? Let's look inside a cat's eye.

First, look at a cat's pupils. The pupil is the black circle in the middle of your eye. Light goes into the eye through it. In bright light, a cat's pupils are very thin, like a line. In the dark, they get much bigger and rounder. A cat's pupils can open wider than ours, so more light gets in.

Second, think about the back of the eye. It has got two kinds of cells for seeing. Some cells work well in bright light and help us see colours. Other cells work better in dim light. Cats have got a lot more of the second kind than people. This makes their eyes more sensitive in the dark.

Third, cats have got a special layer at the back of the eye. It works like a mirror. Light goes through the eye, hits the mirror and comes back again. So the eye uses the same light two times! This is why a cat's eyes shine when you point a torch at them.
Because of all this, a cat needs much less light than a person. Scientists say that a cat can see with only about one sixth of the light that we need. That is why cats are such good hunters at night.

But cat eyes are not better in every way. In the daytime, our eyes are sharper. Things that are far away look clearer to us than to cats. People can also see more colours. Cats see the world in softer, paler colours, a bit like an old photo.

And here is one more surprise. In a room with no light at all, a cat can't see anything. It needs a little light from the moon, the stars or a street lamp. Next time your cat runs around at night, you'll know its secret!

articles.title: My First Day at the Bike Shop
articles.dek: Daniel starts a Saturday job at his uncle's shop. Did everything go well?
paras: Hi Daniel, How was your first day at your uncle's bike shop? Did you like it? Did you fix any bikes? I want to hear everything! I started my job at the pet shop last month, so I know how you feel. The first day is always hard. Write soon! Aisha

Hi Aisha, Thanks for your email. My first day was on Saturday. It wasn't easy! I arrived at eight o'clock, but Uncle Raj wasn't there. He was at the bank. I didn't have a key, so I waited outside in the cold for twenty minutes.

When he came, he gave me a blue work shirt. It was too big, but I didn't say anything. My first job was to clean the bikes. Then I put new tyres on a children's bike. I didn't fix any big problems. Uncle Raj did those himself.

In the afternoon, a woman came into the shop. She wanted a helmet for her son. I didn't know the prices, and I couldn't find the right size. I felt silly! Uncle Raj helped me, and the woman bought a red helmet. Did you make any mistakes on your first day? Daniel

Hi Daniel, Of course I did! On my first day, I gave a customer the wrong fish food. He didn't notice, but his fish didn't eat it. He came back the next day and laughed about it. So don't worry! Did Uncle Raj pay you? Aisha

Hi Aisha, Yes, he did! He gave me thirty pounds. I didn't spend it. I'm saving for a new phone. And guess what? Uncle Raj didn't get angry about the helmet. He said, 'Everybody learns on the job.' I'm going back next Saturday! Daniel

articles.title: Lost in the Museum
articles.dek: Ana is looking at an old map when her class disappears. What can she do?
paras: Last Friday, Ana's class went on a school trip to the city museum. It was a huge old building with tall stone columns. Inside, there were dinosaur bones, Egyptian mummies and a lot of old maps. Ana loved maps, so she was very excited.

At eleven o'clock, the class was standing in the Egypt room. Mr Patel was talking about mummies. But Ana wasn't listening. She was looking at a big old map of the world on the wall. While she was reading the names of the old cities, the class left the room.

When Ana turned round, the room was empty. 'Where is everybody?' she thought. She ran into the next room, but she couldn't see her class. The museum had a lot of rooms and stairs. Ana felt scared. She didn't have a phone with her.

While she was walking down the stairs, she heard a noise. A small boy was sitting on the bottom step. He was crying. 'I can't find my mum,' he said. His name was Sam, and he was five years old. Ana held his hand. 'Don't worry. We'll find her together,' she said.

Ana remembered the information desk near the entrance. They walked there together. A guard was working at the desk. When Ana told him about Sam, he picked up a microphone. 'Can Sam's mum come to the information desk, please?' he said. His voice was very loud in the quiet halls.
Two minutes later, Sam's mum ran to the desk. She was very happy. Then Ana saw someone else. It was Mr Patel! He was looking for Ana when he heard the message.

'Ana! You were lost too!' he said. 'Yes,' said Ana with a smile. 'But I found Sam while I was lost!' Mr Patel laughed. 'Next time, stay with the group,' he said. 'And please look at maps after the trip!'

mindmap.question: How did Ana get lost, and how did she find her class?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the story.
summary.model: Ana got lost in the museum because she was reading a map. But she helped a lost boy, so Mr Patel found her at the information desk.

options.t: Ana was reading a map when her class left the room.
options.why: This is how the problem starts.
options.evidence: While she was reading the names of the old cities, the class left the room.

options.t: Ana found a lost boy and took him to the information desk.
options.why: This is the middle of the story.

options.t: Mr Patel heard the message and found Ana.
options.evidence: He was looking for Ana when he heard the message.

options.t: The museum had dinosaur bones and mummies.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Inside, there were dinosaur bones, Egyptian mummies and a lot of old maps.

options.t: Ana bought a map in the museum shop.
Ana called Mr Patel on her phone.
options.why: Wrong: she didn't have a phone with her.
options.evidence: She didn't have a phone with her.

speak.p: Have you ever visited a museum? What were you doing there, and what did you like?
speak.hint: I went to… / While I was walking around, I saw…

write.p: Look at the idea: a boy was walking in a big shop when he lost his little sister. Write the story in 35 words or more.
steps: Say where the boy was and what he was doing.
Say how he lost his sister.
